utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, you were going to tell us about an exhibit discussed yesterday afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours. I was indebted to Judge Stephen for pointing that out to us because it is very unclear when one looks at the original exhibit and compares it with the translation. We are rather keen to ensure that there is an understanding of that. Might I have your Honour's leave to interpose very quickly a translator that carried out the translation so she can explain why she inserted the words where she did? I think it would be useful if we could do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What exhibit number is that again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 150, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have any objection to our hearing in a very few minutes about this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases, I call Miss Fisek.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Need she be sworn, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Please have a seat. MISS DAHIRA FISEK, called

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you just state your full name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Dahira Fisek.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You are a qualified translator employed in the translation unit of the Tribunal, which unit is under the supervision of the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As part of the duties of the translation unit are documents submitted for translation from various sources including the Defence, the Chambers and Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Niemann, it appears I have a problem getting the transcript up on my screen -- of all the times when we are talking about other technical problems!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good, OK. Mr. Niemann, you have it before you and you can see where we have left off. You may begin again, I would suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I will start with the second question. (To the witness): As part of the duties of the translation unit, are documents submitted for translation from various sources, including the Defence, the Chambers and Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at Exhibit 150? Might that exhibit be shown to the witness? Could you just look at both pages of that exhibit? Looking at the original document in the Serb language and the English translation attached, did you do the English translation from the original document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is the typing on the original document of very poor quality in that it appears that the ribbon on the typewriter at the time the document was created must have been badly worn?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As a consequence of the worn typewriter ribbon, have some of the numbers and words on the document not been reproduced with the carbon imprint of the ribbon on the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: However, in some places has the paper been indented by the typewriter key where it has struck the paper. Although the carbon imprint from the ribbon is not visible, is the indentation on the paper of the key strike visible from the document if it is held to the light?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you translated the original document, could you see some of the typewriter key indentations which you could decipher, and did you include those words and numbers in the translation to the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could see it and I did include them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the word "Dusko", where it appears as the typewriter key indentation on the sixth line from the top of the original document, included in your translation to the English language, and does the word "Dusko" appear on the fifth line from the top of the English translation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you decide to include the word "Dusko" and other words and numbers in a similar circumstance in the English translation as a result of your own decision or were you instructed by any other person to include these letters or words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was my own decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It was your own decision. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. Thank you very much for coming. We appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue with Colonel Selak?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. COLONEL OSMAN SELAK, recalled Examined by MISS HOLLIS, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, you are still under oath. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Miss Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Colonel Selak, at the close of the session yesterday we were talking about the ethnic orientation of the JNA, and I would like to ask you some additional questions concerning that. Did you know a Colonel Vukelic in the Banja Luka area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his position in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel Vukelic was Assistant for Ethics of the Commander of the 5th Corps of the 1st Military District.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was the Military District that you were in in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Colonel Vukelic an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were his duties in his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Assistant for Ethics; prepared morally, ethically the units, maintained relations with the media, with political bodies, socio-political organisations in the area of responsibility of the Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Starting in 1991, did you become aware of statements that Colonel Vukelic was making to the public and the media in which he was making anti-Muslim or anti-Croat remarks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us the type of statements that he was making?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His statements were of a propaganda nature. He expressed belief that the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina was in danger, that it needed to be protected and it all indicated that his need to mobilize the members of the Corps, both the officers and soldiers, for the struggle, as he put it, to save the Serbs from the genocide. His statements appeared in media, in Banja Luka papers, in the paper Glas, on radio and television.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In his statements how did he characterise Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He characterised them as the adversaries of Serbs, preparing genocide over the Serbs, and within this context were his behaviour, his statements.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the end of 1991, do you recall being present at a meeting at which General Vidovic spoke about a new Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes that was on 26th December '91. While submitting the report to the Assistant for the Logistics Commander in Belgrade, one General Vidovic, as the Assistant Commander of the 1st Military District for Ethics and Legal Affairs, stated that Yugoslavia would survive and that within Yugoslavia would be Serb Krajinas and the Republic Serb -- Serb Republic from Bosnia-Herzegovina in addition to other republics.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Vidovic was of what ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What other individuals attended that briefing, to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That briefing with the Assistant Logistics Commander were the Commander of all the Logistics Bases, Rear Bases Corps, and General Vidovic's assistants; at the close of the meeting the Commander of the Military District was also present.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was the Commander of the Military District present when General Vidovic made his remarks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, he was not. He came at the end of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall attending a briefing at the 5th Corps on 1st January 1992, at which briefing the Corps Commander briefed that the JNA now had two tasks before it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the two tasks that the Corps Commander briefed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the first briefing of the new Commander of the 5th Corps of the 1st Military District of General Vidovic who replaced General Uzelac; and at the briefing he said, among other things, that the army had two tasks in these territories, to save the Serbs from the genocide in Croatia and, the second task, to pull out all materiel and equipment from Slovenia and Croatia, the active duty troops, officers and members of families of the military and from the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During that briefing did General Vukovic indicate anything at all about protecting Muslims or Croats from genocide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not a word.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned that Major Pavlovic was one of your escorts starting in the second half of 1991. He was assigned to the 5th Corps at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Pavlovic, my Assistant for Ethics, he was my Assistant in the Command of the Rear Base, but he had been posted there Pavlovic, Jordan Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In late 1991 or 1992 did you become aware of any anti-Muslim or anti-Croat statement that Major Pavlovic was making publicly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say with regard to Major Pavlovic that he was particularly active, especially in instigation in the segment of hatred, anti-propaganda against Muslims and Croats, and he tried to expel them out from the Rear Base of the 5th Corps saying that they were unfit for political or moral reasons or other reasons. At the briefings of my units, he also spoke about the threat to the Serbs. He was one of the most adverse elements in the command of that Base.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The referendum concerning Bosnian independence was held on 29th February and 1st March 1992. Yesterday you mentioned Colonel Cendic during your testimony and indicated that he was your Chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Cendic, Radislav, he was Chief of Staff and Deputy during the preparations for the referendum, and on the day of the referendum he advised, he brought the units together and advised the soldiers how to vote.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did he tell them to vote?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To vote against the referendum, against the independence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn what he had told the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were still honest people, people of integrity. I heard that from soldiers and from superiors and, after all, I was the Commander of that Base and information reached me from the grass roots upward.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992 who was the Commander of the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the spring of '92 from the 28.12.91 to the end was General Vukovic who was then transferred to Nis and was killed in a traffic accident. After that, Major General Momir Talic became the Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After General Talic became Commander of the Corps, did you become aware of General Talic making public statements that were anti-Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Talic pursued the -- implemented the policy of the superior command and the Serb policy. He was not expected to behave otherwise because he would not have become the Commander of the Corps. He would have never been assigned to that duty. He, indeed, tried to mobilize the people, the men. He often addressed the units. He spoke to them about the danger against the Serb people. He first spoke against Slovenia, then against Croatia, that they had broken Yugoslavia apart, and that genocide against the Serb people was that the genocide was threatening the Serb people. His speeches, his addresses, were always in that context.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, to your knowledge, did General Talic meet often with SDS members in the Banja Luka area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Talic had regular briefings with political bodies, notably the SDS. He was a member of the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka. Therefore, he and Colonel Vukelic, his Assistant for Ethics and Head of Security, Colonel Bogavic, were regularly there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to turn now to some questions about the Territorial Defence forces. The Territorial Defence forces were controlled by the republics and the municipalities and were separate from the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From what source did the Territorial Defence forces get their officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was replenished with active duty officers of the Yugoslav People's Army. They were, by and large, men approaching the end of their career, some of failing health.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons did the TO units have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TO units had small arms, light, and they had some mortars, and a few canons of smaller calibres, some anti-infantry mines, hand-made hand bombs, hand grenades, and some were given, some they made themselves, some were given by the JNA at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they also have small arms including automatic weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a weapon that is known as the M48?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is an old Yugoslav rifle or Austro-Hungarian provenance. It was modified by the Yugoslav People's Army and it was updated for the last time in 1948. That is why it is called 48. The calibre is 7.9 millimetres. The TO, for the large part, had precisely those rifles order, automatic weapons; and of late, in the latest years, yes, they did indeed get some automatic rifles when the JNA was replenished, then a smaller number. Some units were issued automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of vehicles did the TO units have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: TO units had heavy vehicles, that is, what opstinas of the republic would purchase from the manufacturers depending on the money, what they could afford, because it was financed by republics and municipalities. So they had civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When we speak of "combat vehicles", what is meant by that term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Combat vehicles means tanks, APCs, reconnaissance vehicles, that is, combat vehicles carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the Territorial Defence units have combat vehicles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who supplied the Territorial Defence with their weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These rifles of 7.9 millimetres and those older automatic weapons which the JNA was discarding from its equipment, it gave them to TO units and the rest of the equipment they had to buy themselves, that is, supply field equipment and whatever these units needed. The army gave them what it was discarding from its formations. We were getting new equipment, new weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the canons and the other heavier type weapons you talked about would have come from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not have heavy weapons. I said smaller calibre canons, yes, that is, older models, older makes and smaller quantities, less than they really needed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those would have come from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were the weapons and materiels that the TO units had, where were those stored?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The TO unit had its storage space which they provided for for themselves and they also had their guards and sentries, their records, their book-keeping. The army had no say in that, nor did it help them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the late 1980s or the early 1990s, did you participate in or become aware of the JNA taking weapons back from the territorial units in the republics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The mid or towards the end of 1990, the order came that the weapons of the Territorial Defence had to be pulled out to the depots of the JNA. In the depots of the Bases, of my Base and other Bases, these weapons were collected as equipment and where there were no Bases these were surrendered to the units of the Corps, Brigades and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons were retrieved from the Territorial Defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All weapons were retrieved from pistols to rifles, to mortars and the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the authority for this action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Federal Assembly passed a law that the Territorial Defence weapons should be returned to the army, the JNA depots, and then these orders were passed on to the Base levels and through the governments of the republics. It was insisted that the weapons should be returned.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this would have been a law from the Federal Assembly of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did all of the republics within the former Yugoslavia comply with this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which republics did not comply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slovenia, Croatia slowed down the tempo of its activities so that in the meantime the Croatian people put up resistance and the formation of the Republic of Croatia took place, and a part of the weapons that was not returned was used for the struggle against the army or, rather, for the acquisition of independence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In Bosnia-Herzegovina, was this order carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During what time period in Bosnia-Herzegovina was this order carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this was completed by the end of 1990, whether one or two municipalities, because this took time, it was necessary to inspect the weapons. I cannot remember exactly the date. I think it was the end of '90, maybe a little into '91. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Subsequent to these weapons being collected from the Territorial Defence forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina, subsequent to that, to your knowledge, were any of these weapons given back to Territorial Defence units or civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that begin to happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This began in '91. At the time of the beginning of the war in Slovenia, later in Croatia, the Federal Assembly, when it took the decision on collection of weapons, authorised the Yugoslav People's Army to be able to approve the issuance of weapons to Territorial Defence units if the Territorial Defence is mobilized; and this precondition was used in the course of '91 to issue through the JNA weapons to some municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 26th December 1992, we have previously spoken of a briefing that you attended. Do you recall during that briefing remarks by General Crmaric during which he gave instructions as to what additional approvals had to be obtained before weapons could be issued to Territorial Defence forces -- I am sorry, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at the briefing for the Assistant Commander of Logistics of the 1st Military District when General Crmaric, Assistant for the rear, in his statement announced, among other things, that units of Territorial Defence cannot be issued weapons without the approval of the Federal Secretariat for national defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This Federal Secretary for National Defence was located where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Crmaric, you said, was Assistant Commander for the rear; what exactly what his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His exact position was Assistant for the rear of the 1st Military District in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this Assistant for Logistics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In fact, after this briefing, Territorial Defence units were given weapons, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only some opstinas or municipalities which were given this approval. I personally did not see this approval because it went to the level of the Corps Commanders. I have not seen it, but I heard about it, and the Commander of the Banja Luka Corps used this right given to him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These units who received the approval from this Federal Secretariat, they were then given weapons by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could I, please, have a document marked as the next in line, I believe that would be Prosecution Exhibit 163 for identification? That does include an English translation. If that could be marked and given to the witness. For Defence reference, that is document 13. (Exhibit 163 was handed to the witness). (To the witness): Colonel Selak, would you please examine that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who is that document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was issued by the command of the Second Military District, representative of the Chief of Staff of the Technical Service, Colonel Gredimir Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To whom is that document being sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is sent to the command of the 5th Corps and the command of the 993rd Logistics Base of which I was the Commander.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the date on the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: February 22nd 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Without going into great detail, would you tell us what is the subject of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document gives orders to the command of the Logistics Base and command of the 5th Corps and on the basis of the orders of the Chief of Staff of the Yugoslav Army for the replenishment of the 3rd Detachment of the 10th Partisan Division of the 5th Corps that weapons should be issued for 76 millimetre ammunition, for 76 millimetre cannon, ammunition for 27 millimetre machine gun, hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, before you go into additional details, I would tender this document as Prosecution Exhibit 163.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 163 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the English translation of that document be put on the overhead projector, please? (To the witness): Sir, you have indicated that this order from Colonel Petrovic was as a result of an order by the General Staff of the JNA, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That the unit to be reinforced was the 3rd Territorial Defence Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the 3rd Detachment of Territorial Defence of the 10th division of the 5th Corps, that was the name, the 3rd Detachment of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was that a Serb unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time could we retrieve Prosecution Exhibit 159? Hesitantly, of course, this is the map with the Krajinas on it, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I promise not to ask a question. We will stick with three.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could that map be put on the overhead, please? (To the witness): Colonel Selak, by pointing at the map on the overhead projector itself, not on your screen, could you please point out for us the area of operation of this 3rd Territorial Defence Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 3rd Territorial Defence Detachment was a part of the 10th Partisan Division located in the region west of Bosanska Gradiska on the Sava River, and the 3rd Detachment was somewhere around Bosanska Dubica and across the Sava River is Jasenovac. Therefore, its direction of operation was Jasenovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, would you please point to the exhibit which is on the overhead projector and just show us in general the area of operation of the 3rd Territorial Defence unit?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of course, we have a problem with the microphone. Colonel Selak, if you can pull that microphone towards you, then maybe we can hear you while you are pointing to the areas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. The area of responsibility of the 10th division and its 3rd Detachment was Sanski Most, Bosanska Dubica, along the Sava River valley.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, sir, this is within the area that is in blue on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If the English version of Prosecution Exhibit 163 could be replaced on to the overhead? Sir, in general, could you tell us what type of munitions were to be supplied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first item, 76 millimetre grenade, and they were piercing grenades, subcalibre grenades, for M18 weapons made in the US. The Yugoslav Army received them somewhere in the 50s from the United States of America. Under (2) from the second ammunition warehouse at Mrkonjic Grad, which is the warehouse of the Logistics Base, the 12.7 millimetre bullet, anti-aircraft and tracer bullets for Browning, hand grenades M75, and 76 millimetre bullets for canon M42 guns, and 76 millimetres for smaller guns.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, you said or the order says that the 3rd Territorial Defence Detachment is part of the 10th Partisan Division. Was the 10th Partisan Division an active duty or a reserve unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Its composition, it was a reserve unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Commander of that division, to your knowledge, would that be an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the 10th division was Colonel Josovic Rade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from Uzice, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would like another document marked. I would ask that this document be marked Prosecution Exhibit 164 for identification. This also includes an English translation. For the Defence reference, this is document 14. (Exhibit 164 was handed to the witness). (To the witness): Colonel Selak, would you please look at that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who is that document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the command of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a name of a person on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the signatory is the Commander of the 2nd Military District, Colonel General Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have known him for almost 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the date on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April 1st 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To whom is that document directed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To units of the 5th Corps and the Logistics Base, Banja Luka. The units of the 5th Corps and the Logistics Base.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Very briefly, could you tell us what the subject of this document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are orders to the Logistics Base of the 5th Corps to issue weapons for units for the Serb Republic and for Territorial Defence units of western Slovenia, launching mechanisms, 20 millimetre guns.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, before you go into details your Honour, I would tender this document as Prosecution Exhibit 164?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 164 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the English translation of that document be put on the projector, please? (To the witness): Colonel Selak, without going into great detail about it, could you tell us in general what types of weaponry are to be provided to the Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are anti-aircraft gun, 20 through 1 millimetre, model 75. That means it was manufactured in 1975, and firing mechanisms for the needs of the Territorial Defence of western Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If 159 could be put again on the overhead projector -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one minute. Is there something -- can you lower that just a little bit? Is it signed by someone?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe he indicated it was signed by General Kukanjac. Could you put the Serbo-Croatian document on the overhead, please, and show the signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecution Exhibit 159 put on the overhead, please? (To the witness): Sir, again pointing to the exhibit on the projector itself, could you show us what area they are discussing when they talk about the Serb area of western Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Western Slavonia, the territory of western Slovenia is coloured here in green. They are the places, localities of Lipik, Pakrac, Nova Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what they mean on this order when they talk about "SRT"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is an abbreviation for means of war, equipment or materiel; that means for replenishing the materiel of Territorial Defence of western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I could have another exhibit marked, please? This would be Prosecution Exhibit 165 for identification. Again it has an English translation. For the Defence, this is document 20. (Exhibit 165 was handed to the witness). (To the witness): Sir, could you please examine that document? That document is from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document is from the command of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a name and a signature that appears at the bottom of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the document was signed by the Commander of the 2nd Military District Colonel General Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To whom is that document being sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The command is sent to the command of the 5th, 9th and 10th Corps of the 2nd Military area, 4th, 5th, 510th and 933rd Logistics Bases.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the date of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April 8th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Very briefly, could you tell us what is the subject of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The contents of the document is that it explains the relocation of units of the Republika Srspka Krajina should be done, and the formation of Logistics Bases of the supreme staff of the Territorial Defence of the Republika Srspka Krajina, and for this reason orders are given for the Logistic Bases in the 2nd Military District to replenish with materiel means as are necessary for the main staff of Territorial Defence of the Republika Srspka Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, before you go into any additional detail, I would like to tender that document as Prosecution Exhibit 165.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 165 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the English translation be put on the projector, please? Sir, the classification of this document is what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document is strictly confidential as a document.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What level classification is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The highest level of classification -- only a State secret is higher than that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, as I understand what you said, this document is addressing the relocation of JNA units from UN safer areas as well as forming Logistics Bases that would be part of a Territorial Defence, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from within the territory of the Republika Srspka Krajina, this was at the time when United Nations were due to arrive to the territory of the Republic of Croatia, and that is why the main staff of Srpska Krajina relocated units to different regions and asked from the General Staff in Belgrade for assistance; and the Commander of the 2nd Military District refers to the order to carry out this task, that is, to form Logistic Bases of Territorial Defence of the Republic of Srpska Krajina, to replenish them from the Rear Bases of the JNA of the 2nd Military District, and for all the expenses of the relocation and replenishment to be covered by the Logistics Bases or the 2nd Military District or the Secretariat of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, is it paragraph 2 which directs the 2nd Military District to replenish or supply the Territorial Defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Point (2) explains that. Do I have to quote it?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, you do not. Is it paragraph (6) that indicates who will bear the cost of supplying these Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This would be the JNA that would bear that cost?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, through the Logistic Bases because they had certain resources and materiel reserves, and they would cover part of the expenses out of their own budgets and a part from the Defence Department. That was the regular system as it functioned.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if I could have you look at Prosecution Exhibit 159, if that could be put on the elmo again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that this order discusses the establishment of Logistics Bases, Territorial Defence Logistics Bases, in Republika Srpska Krajina. Could you please for the court point to the Republika Srpska Krajina area on that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Republika Srspka Krajina is coloured in green. It is situated on the territory of the Republic of Croatia. The 405th Logistics Base mentioned in these orders were situated in Knin. Other Bases to which orders are issued for formation, I do not know exactly their locations, but they themselves came for these supplies. Part of the equipment, materiel, was to be put in storage which was to be sealed for UN Nations to be able to inspect them. I personally was in Nova Gradiska, the penitentiary there which was used as storage space for this Logistic Base of the Republika Srspka Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, then the Territorial Defence units that would have been receiving supplies would have been Serb units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if those exhibits, both Prosecution Exhibits 159 and 165, could be retrieved and provided to the Registrar, please? (To the witness): Colonel Selak, you mentioned yesterday that Territorial Defence units in Jajce, Mrkonjic Grad and Sipovo received weapons from you. Could you tell us when they got those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but it could have been October or November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall with certainty that it was in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Other than Jajce, which I believe you mentioned was a mixed Territorial Defence unit, do you know of any other groups that contained non-Serbs that were given weapons by the JNA in the end of 1991 or in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Weapons were issued in the municipalities, Sipovo, Mrkonjic, Jajce, but in 1992 a delegation of Jajce Serbs came to request weapons from me because they were in danger to defend themselves from Muslims and Croats. I did not give them those weapons because it was a paramilitary formation. I told them that I would accept that people come to my depot in Jajce, that they could put on the uniform and then they would be issued weapons, but then they would have to become a military, to be in the barracks as normal units, as regular units. They refused it and then the polemics ensued with the Corps Commander and they did not get the weapons -- at least not from me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you later learn that they had received weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They all received weapons, all the Serbs who reported to the units, because the strength of the Corps indicated some illogical things, the formation strength and the actual number of people who came for meals, who applied for their rations or weapons indicated that almost all people in that area were armed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, by late spring of 1992, with the exception of, perhaps, Jajce which may have been a mixed unit, the Territorial Defence units who were being given weapons by the JNA were of what ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In '92 those were exclusively Serb formations replenished with Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have testified that Territorial Defence units that were mobilized were entitled to get weapons from the JNA. In the spring of 1992, did you become aware of any irregularities that were occurring in the call-up of Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those units made part of the Corps. We in our command of the Base did not know their exact number, composition or deployment. The request for the replenishment in men or weaponry, the Corps submitted to the Base and it was then issued and placed them, issued to people, and they were then placed under their command. Muslims and Croats did no longer come to request them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall a meeting in April 1992 at which the Chairman of the Municipal Assembly of Donji Vakuf complained of irregularities in the call up of Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A meeting was held, I believe, on April 13th 1992 in the municipality Donji Vakuf in the office of the Mayor, Mr. Kemal Cajic. It was attended also by the Mayor of Bugojno municipality, I believe his name was Vlado Solic, and the meeting was also attended by Colonel Stanislav Galic, the Commander of the 13th Partisan Division of the 5th Corps, also attended the meeting with my two assistants.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that Colonel Galic -----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry, but the answers of the witness, the last two answers, do not seem to relate to mobilization, although your question is irregularities in mobilization.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I believe he will speak about a complaint about irregularities in mobilization.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I see. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Colonel Selak, you indicated that Colonel Galic was the Commander of what units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 30th Partisan Division of the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did the Chairman of the Municipal Assembly complain to Colonel Galic about irregularities in the call-up of Territorial Defence units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At their meeting, the President of the municipality, Mr. Terzic, said that the Secretariat for National Defence of the Municipal Assembly of Donji Vakuf, headed by a Serb, had taken away the files of the TO unit of Donji Vakuf, that Muslims had not been called up and that that was irregular.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Colonel Galic have any response to this complaint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Galic replied that, in fact, only volunteers were reporting, and that his representative had been to the Secretariat for National Defence, and he thought that everything was regular regarding that matter. Terzic repeated again that the Muslims had not been called up because the Serbs had the files.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall Colonel Galic making any statement that Federal directives must be followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, towards the end of his statement Colonel Galic said that Federal regulations needed to be respected and that was why the army was there, to see that the Federal regulations are respected, and that was also the reply regarding the manner of mobilization.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What Federal directives was Colonel Galic referring to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He meant the regulations saying that the order for the TO mobilization is issued by the General Staff of the JNA, and there was no further discussion about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Galic, was he a regular officer, an active duty officer or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was he from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the area of Banja Luka in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The unit, the 30th Partisan Division, was this an active duty unit or a reserve units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A reserve unit formed in '91 and made of active duty officers pulled out from Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was a JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the JNA and the Territorial Defence Forces, the court has heard reference made to the militia. Does the word "militia" mean "civilian police"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these civilian police divided into an active and a reserve component?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was the JNA normally responsible for providing weapons, uniforms and equipment to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1991 and 1992, did the JNA begin to issue weapons, equipment and uniforms to police units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did this begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my knowledge, in the spring of '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to have an exhibit marked as the Prosecution exhibit next in line; I believe that would be Prosecution Exhibit 166 for identification. This also includes an English translation. For Defence reference, this is document 23. (Exhibit 166 was handed to the witness). (To the witness): Sir, would you please look at this document? Who is this document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document is from the Commander of the 2nd Military District.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In April 1992, what Military District did you belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 2nd Military District in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was the Banja Luka Corps, the 5th Corps, also then a member of the 2nd Military District?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a person's name and signature that appears on this document, the last page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the document was signed by the Commander of the 2nd Military District, Commander Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us very briefly what the subject of this document is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document says that the Commander of the 2nd Military District had received from the Ministry of the Interior of the Serb Republic Bosnia-Herzegovina a request for the transfer of the materiel and equipment for the special police task force at the State Security Centre in Banja Luka. This -- it means the wide range of equipment and materiel from helicopters to armoured vehicles, to heavy duty vehicles, to weapons, from pistols to machine guns, ammunition and explosives, signals, equipment, signalling equipment, sets, instruments, a special -----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, before you continue, please, I would tender this exhibit as Prosecution Exhibit 166.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 166 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Colonel Selak, would you please look at page 4 of that document, the second sentence which indicates December of 1992. Is that correct, or would that have been a typographic error? Would that have been December 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a mistake. It is 30th December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, do not -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Colonel, do not change it. Do not change the exhibit before you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, no, I will not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, at this time of this document and this request, what would have been the ethnic composition of the special police force in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A member of it was a Muslim or a Croat. They were exclusively Serb. They could not be in that unit, only the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does that document contain a support by the Commander that this request be approved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last sentence is explicit. It recommends to meet the request notably for things which cannot be obtained on the market and that means weaponry, ammunition and the rest -- that could not be found in the market or, at least, a very small share.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, is there any portion of that document which would enable you to determine how many special police personnel were going to be supplied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, before you ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According -----

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: -- go into that, could you tell us what page you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that English translation could be put on the overhead? (To the witness): Sir, I am sorry for interrupting. Could you go ahead and tell us how you know the number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the supplies on page 3, item 64, camouflage uniform, 157 pieces. This indicates the strength of the unit ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- because each member had to have a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, do you recall in the spring of 1992 supplying any such materials to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was carried out, the orders arrived and we had to comply with them. The Rear Base did not have all these supplies, so only what was available at the Base was supplied. I do not know who supplied the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that exhibit could be retrieved and provided to the Registrar? (To the witness): Colonel Selak, we have talked a bit about call ups or mobilization of Territorial Defence forces. I would like to ask you some more questions about mobilization. First, I would like to talk about mobilizations of JNA forces, reserve forces, in 1991. In May 1991, do you recall any type of mobilization of forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the fighting in Croatia started some time in early May '91, the orders came about partial mobilization of the 5th Corps, an armoured Battalion, that is, was to be mobilized and sent to Kupres south of Banja Luka in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know about how many personnel were actually mobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two units mobilized; one, that is Battalion, had about 250 men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So there would have been about 500 men mobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those two Battalions; one had 250 and the armoured battalion -- the battalion's tanks were taken from the secondary military school for armoured mechanized units in order not to use the Brigade, relevant Brigade, of the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, to your knowledge, these 500 or so men who were mobilized in May 1991, were they ever demobilized after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have that information. I think that the superiors who then sent one of these battalions to Plitvica, one to Kupres and I think they were subordinate to Sarajevo -- they were accountable to Sarajevo directly, because Novi Travnik and that area down there was under direct Sarajevo jurisdiction and this battalion accounted directly to them. It was never demobilized. There was no reason for that. We supplied -- I had formed a Logistics platoon which was sent to Kupres and which supported them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to this May partial mobilization, were there additional mobilizations in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On September 15th 1991 the mobilization orders arrived to the 5th Corps, to the Rear Base, and I think that the rocket Base also received orders for mobilization.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this mobilization a partial mobilization or was this an order for a full mobilization?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was full mobilization.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From whom did you receive the order to mobilize the forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Commander of the 1st Military District in Belgrade to which we were subordinated at the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was in 1991, and you were still a part of the 1st Military District?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the stated purpose of this mobilization?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The purpose of the mobilization was because the Corps was subsequently engaged in the territory of west Slavonia, Dubica, Jasenovac, and that was why the mobilization was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So they would have been mobilized to take part in the fighting in Croatia against Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know how many people in your area were mobilized as a result of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We, I mean, in the Base command to stock all the strength daily because the units were sending in their requests for food and they showed their strength; so that immediately after the initial days of the mobilization the Corps grew from 4500 to over 15,000 men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When these men would be mobilized, did they immediately get weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, whenever the mobilization would take place the weapons were issued immediately in the first hours after the mobilization. We called it uniting men with arms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then these mobilized men would keep these weapons until they were demobilized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When these reserve units were mobilized, did they come under the command of the active duty military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence units when they were mobilized, did they come under the command of the active duty military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At the level of Brigade and higher battalions, when there were no active duty officers, then the vacancies were filled with reserve duties, but TO Detachments and Brigades, yes, had active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mentioned a mobilization order you received on 15th September 1991. After that date, were you present at a meeting where formation of new light brigades was discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was at a meeting when -- the meeting was chaired by General Adzic, Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army. The meeting was attended by the Commander of 5th Corps, General Nikola Uzelac, General Raseta from Zagreb of the 5th Military District, several officers of the Knin Corps, and then there were echelons of the command of the Banja Luka Corps and myself as the Commander of the Logistics Base. At the meeting, General Adzic said that so-called light brigades needed to be formed numbering 800 to 1,000 men armed with light infantry weapons, mortars, mines, explosive devices -- they mean mines and bombs -- that these brigades have to be highly mobile and that they would be deployed by the vehicles of the Corps. That was the first official statement about the formation of light brigades, and shortly after that the formation began at an accelerated pace.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, would these be active duty or reserve units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As soon as mobilization was over there was no difference between the reserve and active duty. It was a unit like any other, armed, equipped, and while perhaps its training for operations could be questionable.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Commanders of these light brigades, would they be active duty or reserve Commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I knew, they were all active duty superiors because a large number of officers had arrived from Slovenia and Croatia, so that it was not difficult to fill in commanding posts with these men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then the weapons for these light brigades would be supplied by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this meeting you said that these light brigades began to be formed. To your knowledge, were there any such light brigades formed in the Banja Luka area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every municipality, every opstina, smaller such as Mrkonjic or Jajce and others, the population of about 10,000 formed one Brigade each; Banja Luka formed four; Prijedor two; Sanski Most two. I think that other places, I am talking about Bosnia and Krajina, I think that other localities had one Brigade each only, and they were all accountable to the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, of the light brigades with which you were familiar, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic composition of these light brigades?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Going back again to this 15th September order that you received ordering mobilization, did that order also order you to prepare to store weapons and equipment you would receive from Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand, could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, I am sorry. You have spoken about receiving an order on 15th September 1991, a mobilization order. Did that order also include instructions for you to prepare to store weapons and equipment you would be receiving from Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons and equipment did you, in fact, receive from Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slovenia and Croatia, JNA units were pulling out virtually everything, from equipment -- from weaponry to equipment, to computer equipment, to supplies. Up to 40 freight carriages arrived in Banja Luka daily. They were even sending office furniture which came as a surprise. There were also car trains with weaponry and equipment. A major part of that was directly sent both by trains and by road to Serbia Montenegro. I am referring to what arrived to the territory of the Rear Base in Banja Luka, and that we did not have enough storage space. The equipment was received in the open, and at a certain point there was a risk of fire, of explosion, and then it was ordered to send on immediately part of that equipment to Serbia Montenegro, which we did. Some of the equipment the Corps took for itself. We were never able to keep any books about that because the records, the book-keeping, allegedly was done by the Corps. The equipment, of course, had to be controlled to see that it was in working order, the ammunition and my ammunition and weapons specialist did it around the clock. I do not know who else did that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you continue to receive such military weapons and equipment until the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I understand your testimony correctly, you stored as much of that materiel as you could safely do so in your own storage facilities and then the rest of that materiel you sent on to Serbia and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were other routes. I am referring to the area of responsibility of my Rear Base, but I know that the same thing was done by the Sarajevo Logistics Base with headquarters in Mostar, that there were also transports using maritime routes or railways to Zagreb, Vinkovci, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These weapons and equipment that you received and stored, what did you do with this materiel? Did you use it within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we used them for the regular replenishment of units in the area of responsibility of the Rear Base. After the storage, technical control, if they were in working order, then of course we issued them normally for the replenishment of the units when they applied for them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So as mobilizations were being carried out, they would have been provided with weapons and equipment in part from these stores?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You spoke earlier of a meeting in December 1991 at which General Vidovic talked about the new Yugoslavia. At this same meeting, do you recall General Crmaric briefing that he had supplied 150,000 weapons and 200,000 complete sets of uniforms and equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Assistant Commander for Logistics was General Crmaric, and in his statement he said that to replenish the units of the 1st Military District which had been mobilized -- they were mobilized in Bosnia, Sarajevo, Banja Luka and in Tuzla, and I believe some units around Novi Sad had also been mobilized -- that they had issued 150,000 pieces of small arms and 250,000 uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your reaction to this briefing item?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This came rather as a surprise to me because I knew that the 1st Military District unit had been supplied with weapons and uniforms and equipment, so that those 150,000 and 250,000 uniforms meant that new men had been mobilized for other formations and not only for JNA units. That was the logical conclusion that, perhaps, a certain number of uniforms, perhaps this difference between 150,000 and 250,000 uniforms, perhaps it was those who had not responded to mobilization, Muslims and Croats, because uniforms were kept at home. They were issued, those uniforms, and they were kept ought home because of the speed of the mobilization and I thought that, perhaps, 250,000 were to fill in up to the number because the Croats and Muslims would respond, but 150,000 pieces of weaponry, that must have meant new men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be, perhaps, a good point to break?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we will stand in recess for 20 minutes. Colonel, speak a little more slowly, if you can, please, because the interpreters have to translate it for us and it is a little difficult for them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Colonel Selak, in April or May 1992 was there another mobilization in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Microphone, please).

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, would you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In April '92 -- I am afraid the question was not clear.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Was the mobilization in April '92 that you have asked?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me state that question again. In April or May 1992, was there another mobilization in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. In addition to mobilizations, did your area also have an influx of soldiers and officers from outside the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, up to May 15th all soldiers doing their service had to withdraw from JNA units who were born in Serbia or Montenegro. They had to return to Serbia or Montenegro by that date. At the same time, soldiers born in Bosnia-Herzegovina who were doing their service in units of the JNA in Serbia and Montenegro had to come to Bosnia-Herzegovina and to report to units and place themselves at the disposal of JNA units in Bosnia. If that was what you were referring to in your first question, those soldiers did not come to -- did come to units, including my own Base.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to this relocation of personnel, were there also personnel coming into your area from Slovenia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Slovenia and Croatia units were coming, both complete units and commanding officers, officers, non-commissioned officers, individually who were pulling out of Slovenia and Croatia and who placed themselves at the disposal of JNA units in Bosnia-Herzegovina, including Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As of the beginning of June 1992, how many men were you supporting in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of June 1992, the Banja Luka Corps had on its list for meals, for rations, 78,000 and several hundred people. This number does not include two brigades, I think, Skender Vakuf and Sipovo, nor does it include the so-called Doboj group with 15,000 men, and it does not include 22,000 men of the 2nd Corps of the army of the Republika Srspka with the command in Drvar, so the Drvar Corps is not included in that number.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you were to include all of these other units, how many men were you supplying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Without the Rear Base, about 120,000, 119,800 and something.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: 119,000 and something?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I take it that means 119,000 and something?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Probably close to 120,000 maybe is what you are saying, Colonel Selak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, what was the size of a peace time Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Banja Luka Corps in peace time, it was called the 5th Corps, in peace time numbered 4,500 men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the wartime strength, a typical wartime strength, for the 5th Corps in ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In peace time?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: -- wartime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Wartime, it covered the area of Bosnian Krajina with the exception of its western part, 80,000 people plus the Doboj group, plus these two opstinas in my estimate a force of about four normal Corps, because the Drvar Corps numbered 22,000 men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, these approximate 120,000 men that you were supplying, these supplies were provided within the military chain of command, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, under the 5th Corps, later the 1st Krajina Corps, included all these units with the exception of the 2nd Krajina Corps of Drvar which numbered 22,000 men and it was directly subordinated to the Chief of Staff of the Banja Luka, so that the Banja Luka Corps had about 100,000.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, I would like to now ask you some questions about paramilitary activity. In your position in the JNA, did you become aware of any paramilitary units operating within your area in either 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we called them "red beret"s because they were wearing red berets on their heads. They were officially called Serb Defence Forces. The command was in the Hotel Bosna in Banja Luka. They were trained at the training grounds of Manjaca. A second military, paramilitary, formation I am aware of was the formation of Milanovic from Prnjavor. They were called "Eagles" or something like that. I saw them in '92 at a locality near Prnjavor. They did not look nice at all. They were armed with rifles and knives and they were selling a picture -- or they gave the impression of special task forces.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to ask you some questions about these red berets. You indicated they were being trained at Manjaca. Was this at the JNA training area in Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was the training area for the training of tank units near Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were they being trained there by JNA personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was supplying them with weapons, equipment and uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the person in charge was Colonel Subotic Bogdan, Assistant Commander of the Educational Centre for Armoured Rear Units. He went there often and we knew that he was the main organiser. Later, he became Minister of the Army of the Republika Srspka. I do not know any other officers personally, but I know they were active duty officers at the training grounds.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, Colonel Subotic, he was an active duty officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were the red berets receiving weapons, equipment and uniforms from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not receive them from the Logistics Base of Banja Luka. I believe that they received them from the Corps or from the Educational Centre where Subotic was an Assistant Commander, but not from my unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you first learn that these red berets were being trained at the Manjaca area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of that; I was in the office of the Commander of the 5th Corps, General Uzelac, when he was called up by Colonel Subotic and they spoke on the phone. Both of them were due to visit the training grounds to see the training and, from that conversation and the details I heard, I assessed that some units were being trained that certainly did not belong to the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was it that you heard this conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was November '91. At that time and from that conversation, Uzelac asked me later, what was Subotic's name, and so I assessed that the two of them did not know each other and later on they became very intimate and close.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall a briefing you attended in May at which this training of paramilitary units at Manjaca was discussed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at a meeting with the Commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, General Talic, there was talk and Talic said that all paramilitary formations had to go from the training ground -- I think this must have been 28th May -- that all paramilitary formations had to be removed from Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Talic at this time had become the Commander of the Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had mentioned earlier that a detention camp was established at the Manjaca training area. Do you recall a meeting that you attended at which General Talic spoke about establishing this detention camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was a meeting with General Talic on June 1st '92 when, among other things, he ordered that all soldiers at the training ground of Manjaca should be armed, and that preparations be carried out for the formation of a prisoner of war camp for 2,000 men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were taskings given out at that meeting to establish this camp?
