utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why, were any officers tasked at this meeting to carry out any preparations to establish the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the details. It was the duty of the Chief of Staff of the Corps command and his assistants. I cannot remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this meeting at which establishment of the camp was discussed before or after the meeting at which General Talic indicated the paramilitary units must leave Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the meeting on 28th May, Talic ordered that paramilitary formations had to leave Manjaca. At the time I did not understand why, but probably because of the impending formation of the prisoner of war camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said earlier that a Lieutenant Colonel Popovic had been returned to active duty and became the Commander of the camp. Was he on active duty with the military while he was commanding that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel Bozo Popovic, he was Lieutenant Colonel in retirement. I do not know when the order came for his reactivation, but immediately after formation of the camp he was appointed Commander of that camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time he had been recalled to active duty with the military, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, in the spring of 1992, did the paramilitary units in the Banja Luka area come under the command of the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to turn now to the subject of the supposed JNA withdrawal from Bosnia-Herzegovina. You indicated that in May 1992 officers were to relocate. We have heard testimony that in May 1992 the JNA was to withdraw from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall a briefing you attended on 18th May 1992 at which the Commander of the Banja Luka Corps briefed that on that date the new army was in place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this 18th May 1992 briefing the Commander of the Banja Luka Corps was General Talic, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this briefing do you recall a request being discussed, a request by the Serb Krizni Stab or Crisis Staff Committee, for the military to open a corridor to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. At the briefing with General Talic, among other things, the request was made to ensure a corridor for road transport from Banja Luka in the direction of Serbia. That corridor was essential for supplying units of the army of the Republika Srspka, and my Base used it, in particular, for bringing in materiel from Serbia and Montenegro, armaments and equipment, and that is why that corridor was essential. It was the only land connection from western Bosnia in the direction of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, to your knowledge, did the Commanders at that meeting support that request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May what had been the JNA was now supposedly two separate armies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina or, rather, the Republika Srspka there was only one army, and that was now the army of the Republika Srspka because the Republika Srspka had been officially proclaimed and its army as well. The insignia were changed on the caps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The other part of the JNA that was now in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, what was that army now called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was now officially called the army of Yugoslavia, and it had the sign "VJ".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska, was the acronym for that army the "VRS"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The army of the Republika Srspka or "VRS" in short.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, when you became an officer in the JNA, did you have to take an oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you took that oath as an officer in the JNA, to whom did you swear your loyalty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the peoples of Yugoslavia and the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When this supposed split occurred and the VRS and the VJ emerged, did you take a new oath to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, on 18th May 1992 when officially the army of the Republika Srpska was proclaimed, on May 20th I submitted a request for retirement.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, between that date and the date in July when you left your active duty, between those dates, did you ever take an oath to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, and I would not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know of any of the officers who had been in the JNA and were now in the VRS who took a new oath of office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not heard of such an oath. I have not been present. There was some talk about an oath. Nobody tried to ask me to do that. I would not. I know they went to church. Whether they took an oath, I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time of this requested withdrawal or supposed withdrawal of the JNA, to your knowledge, were there instances where the Bosnian government, the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, attempted to block the withdrawal of JNA troops or assets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my area of responsibility, some minor attempts of putting up barricades were made, but not -- I know there were some cases in Sarajevo, Tuzla, Mostar -- in Banja Luka this did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In these instances, these attempts to block the withdrawal, why were they doing that? What were they trying to prevent, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tried to prevent the pull out of equipment of the Yugoslav People's Army from Bosnia-Herzegovina for Serbia and Montenegro, equipment and materiel and armaments.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, I would now like to ask you a series of questions dealing with the military both before and after 18th May 1992. First, I would like to talk to you about pay for military members before and after this date. Sir, before 18th May 1992, who paid the active duty component of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army, the General Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, after this date, 18th May 1992, by whom were the active duty military members of the VRS paid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also by the army of Yugoslavia or, rather, by the Federal Government as was called.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are referring to the Federal Government in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, you yourself, by whom are you paid after 18th May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the Federal Government in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall attending a briefing in June 1992 at which General Djukic said that the Federal Government would continue to finance the VRS as it was on 19th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at a meeting with the Assistant for Logistics of the Commander of the General Staff of the Republika Srspka -- his name was Djukic Djordje -- also present were Logistics Assistants of the Banja Luka Corps, of the Air Force, of the army of the Republika Srspka, the Chiefs of Staff of Corps and Logistic Bases, and the question was raised of the payment of services, materiel and of officers. General Djukic declared that the Federal Government would continue to finance this army, as he said, with the numerical strength of officers as registered on May 19th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So he indicated at that time that the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia would continue to pay for the needs of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He explicitly said "this army" thinking of the army of the Republika Srspka to which it belonged, and that pay would be received by the active duty officers as registered on May 19th, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that at this time General Djukic was the Assistant for Logistics of the General Staff of the VRS. What had been his prior position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Djukic completed the Military Technical Academy in Zagreb. His last post was Chief of Staff of the Technical Administration of the Yugoslav People's Army in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Glamoc in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Before 18th May 1992, where were your personnel records kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which records do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your military personnel records.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My own personal file was in Belgrade in the personnel administration of the Federal Secretariat of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 where was this file kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It remained in the same place where it was before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, you have testified that in 1991 the JNA Logistics organisation was reorganised into 16 Logistics Bases?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And that your Base was one such Base?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That in 1991 you were in the 1st Military District which was headquartered in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And that in 1992 you became part of the 2nd Military District which was headquartered in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as of January 10th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about your Logistics area of operations and procedures prior to 18th May and after 18th May. You have previously been shown your area of responsibility before 18th May. That was marked as Prosecution Exhibit 161. After 18th May, did your AOR change and become larger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would like an exhibit marked as Prosecution Exhibit 167 for identification. For the Defence, this will be map No. 2. (Exhibit 167 was handed to the witness) (To the witness): Sir, if you could look at that exhibit.?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does this exhibit show your area of responsibility as it expanded after 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender this as Prosecution Exhibit 167.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 167 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could that exhibit be put on the projector, please. Sir, looking at this exhibit, is the area within the solid red line your area of responsibility beginning after 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The towns within this area are towns where you actually delivered supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you point out for us, please, where the expansion of your area of responsibility occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The expansion of the area of responsibility applies to the eastern part Teslic, Doboj and Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, this expansion in this area was the result of combat with the military units you supplied and what other ethnic group or groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an expansion of military operations of the Banja Luka corps eastward towards Doboj, Modrica and Teslic where operations were being conducted against the Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to offer the next exhibit in line which would be Prosecution Exhibit 168 for identification. For the Defence this will be document 9 in the order of documents. (Exhibit 168 was handed to the witness). Colonel Selak, is this document an indication of flow chart of your logistics procedures and chain of command before 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this document prepared by personnel in the Office of the Prosecutor based upon your instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender that document as Prosecution Exhibit 168.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 168 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that document could be put on the overhead, please. The document is somewhat daunting when you first look at it. Could you tell us, Colonel Selak, the red lines on the document, do these red lines signify authority or approval in your logistics procedures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, from the superior towards the subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to the 18th May that would flow from the JNA General Staff downward, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, down to the level of Brigades, Battalions and Companies.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, do the green lines on this document signify the flow of materiels downward to the subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means the operationalization of supplies from bases of the technical administration, contracting supply to rear bases, to corps, to bases of brigades, and then to battalions and companies. So the setup of the logistic supply.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, the blue lines that appear on this flow chart, do those blue lines signify the flow of request for materiel beginning at the lower echelons as the requests move upward?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the blue line indicates applications, requests for logistics support from company up to the level to base and army command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, Colonel Selak said he submitted his resignation on 20th May 1992. This chart was drawn during that period or after 18th May? How long was he in this position after 18th May?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. His testimony, if I could make an offer of proof as to his testimony, will be that he submitted his resignation then. He actually remained in his active duty position until 10th or the middle of July 1992 and his retirement was actually effective 30th September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, do you, your base, the 993rd base ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 10th July, not June, 10th July.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. If I said June I misspoke; it was July. Colonel Selak, your base, the 993rd Rear Base, that is depicted here as the Rear Service Base which is just below the army command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was the executive body of the army command, the executive body in the logistics sense.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The rear service base, that is where you fit, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this chart, it appears that requests go -- if you could move that chart down a bit so we could see the top of the chart, please -- it appears that requests will go from your base, looking at my left on the chart, to what are marked as local contracts and contracted suppliers. What types of materiel would you receive from these individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Yugoslav Army concluded contracts with companies in Yugoslavia manufacturing different kinds of equipment that it did not manufacture itself. There were annual contracts and longer term contracts from food stuffs to other supplies and even parts of armaments.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, these contracted suppliers, were any of those located in Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 did you continue to receive supplies from those contracted suppliers located in Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Looking to my right on the chart it appears that you also make requests to what has been marked "Technical Administration". Could you tell us what type of materiels you would receive through Technical Administration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Technical Administration or the Federal Secretariat for National Defence incorporated as its executive body the Technical Administration base, and through it all the imported materiel and equipment went, that is imported from other countries. That base distributed down to the rear bases of the Yugoslav People's Army as shown here on the chart.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, what types of materiel would it be that would be imported?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the armaments and equipment not manufactured in Yugoslavia, ammunition for virtually all for the ground forces that was not manufactured in the country and was needed from ground to ground, missiles to other weapons which were not manufactured by the Yugoslav Army and yet were needed by it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, after 18th May 1992 did you continue to deal with this Technical Administration when you needed such types of materiel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I maintained permanent contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you indicated earlier that this Technical Administration was located in Serbia and Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May what change occurred in this flow, this logistics flow, as far as your chain of command was concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The changes consisted in that requests had now to go through the Chief of Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska which collected information from other bases and other parts, and they were put there and the organisation went through Belgrade for that part of materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, you would then have been in this rear service base subordinate to what became the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, in terms of your everyday practical working of the logistics system, were there any changes for you after 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only change was that the command of units and bases was now the main staff of the Republika Srpska in Pale. Otherwise it remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 did you have occasion to speak with logistics personnel in the VRS, logistics personnel at higher headquarters levels?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked to General Djukic, Assistant for Logistics.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you speak with him on the telephone concerning logistics matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you know, what was the area prefix for his telephone number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Area code?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, the first three numbers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, that was the area code for what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The area of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now to your knowledge, was he physically located in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was at Pale in the main staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of why then he had this Belgrade prefix for his phone number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some officers had been given direct lines, Belgrade/Pale. There was a link there and it was used in everyday communication because there was a need for direct communication between the Chief of Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would make these phone calls to General Djukic you would be in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you would call him by going through a phone number through Belgrade and they would connect you down to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, his secretary would answer and then she would connect me to his number, to his telephone.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions now about the chain of command for logistics. Around the time of the ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Before you leave that chart, would it be possible for the witness to show where on the chart the change took place when the Army of Republika Srpska started giving the direct orders?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, I believe that that will be shown on the chart we have showing the actual chain of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, around the time of this supposed withdrawal of the JNA, what official message was given to Serb officers from outside Bosnia regarding whether they should remain in Bosnia or leave Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The message was that they could leave the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but nobody did for practical reasons. If I may, I will explain what those reasons were?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A larger number of officers who had withdrawn from Slovenia and Croatia were moving towards Belgrade, towards Yugoslavia, and they were facing housing problems, jobs for their wives or children. The officers who were serving in Bosnia, whereas were born IN Serbia, had their housing problem solved or education of their children and employment for their children. That is they had another motive. In addition to, as I said, fighting for Serbhood they also had practical reasons why they did not go there. They were receiving their pay regularly as if they had been in Yugoslavia and any other fringe benefits such as health insurance and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What about NCOs, were they being encouraged to leave as well, at least officially encouraged to leave as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same applied as to the officers. They also stayed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they also stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to show you what has been marked, should be marked next in line as Prosecution Exhibit 169 for identification. I would ask that it be so marked and provided to the witness. For Defence purposes this is document 10 in the order of documents. (Exhibit 169 was handed to the witness). Sir, does that document depict your logistics chain of command prior to 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 169.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 169 will be admitted. Is that prior to May 18th?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. If that could be put on the overhead projector, please. Sir, if we look at the top of this -- could you move it up just a little bit, please -- prior to 18th May 1992 you would have reported to Major General Ratko Milicevic who was the Assistant Commander for Logistics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Commander of the Second Military District in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From him the chain of command went upward to General Kukanjc who was the Commander of the Second Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From there it went up to the JNA General Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time the Chief of the General Staff was General Adzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, General Blagoje Adzic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Djukic is here with an arrow towards the Technical Administration, a black. He was head of the Technical Administration at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was the head of the Technical Administration.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you look at this chain of command at this time, how many of the officers shown on this chain of command are active duty officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the officers indicated here are active duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you look at this chain of command now, how many of the officers shown on this chain of command are non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this chain of command I am not one and Mujo Camic head of the Technical Service in the rear base. All the others are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, on this exhibit there appear two red Xs below some names. Do those red Xs signify officers who were either from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these red markings, two of them indicate that they are Serbs from Serbia or Montenegro and just one red mark is that they are Serbs outside Serbia from Croatia or perhaps Macedonia or I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you look at this exhibit some of the Serbian officers have no marks under their names, no Xs. Does that signify that those officers, to your knowledge, were from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are Serbs from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now I would like to look at the chain of command after this 18th May date. I would ask that this exhibit be marked Prosecution Exhibit 170 for identification and provided to the witness. This would be document 11 in the order of documents. (Exhibit 170 was handed to the witness). If the witness would retain 169, please, and if 170 could now be examined by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, is this your logistics chain of command after 18th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender this document as Prosecution Exhibit 170.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 170 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could that document please be placed on the elmo and if the witness could be provided Prosecution Exhibit 169 for reference. Sir, looking at this document, your chain of command now goes to the VRS command, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Under that command now you would be reporting to Major General Djukic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So then General Djukic has moved down from being the head of technical administration to being the Assistant Commander for Logistics for the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now this dotted line on the chart, does this signify that there was no formal chain of command between the VRS and the VJ Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this document could you tell us of the officers shown on that document how many officers are active duty officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them are active duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Of these officers how many of these officers are non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The remaining non-Serbs, I am alone, I am the only one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, is that because Lieutenant Colonel Camic has been replaced by Major Spiric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mujo Camic was replaced and Major Spiric came to head the Technical Service of the command of the logistic base.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this chain of command now after 18th May, after this division of the armies, do the double red Xs again signify officers who are from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you see any single red Xs on this chart?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are Colonel Tapsic and nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That signifies that Colonel Tapsic is a Serb either from Croatia or Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel Tapsic is a Serb from Dvor na Uni in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then the other Serb officers under whose name no X appears, these are Bosnian-Serb officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, there are dates under the names of some of these officers. What do these dates signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These dates signify until what year they occupied that specific post.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Judge Stephen, did that answer your prior question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes, splendidly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have a question regarding Exhibit 169. If you can just put it back or perhaps you can answer this question, Colonel Selak. Are there any non-Serbs on 169 other than yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were myself and Lieutenant Colonel Mujo Camic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Both of you do not have a symbol under your name. I see over here to the left, though, General Talic. That would indicate he is a Serb from Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But the only reason I know that, I suppose, is that we have heard testimony about him, so we understand that he is a Serb, but he does not have anything under his name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour I thought ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you explained it well, except you did not indicate for 169 who was a non-Serb. You did for 170.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour, I thought I had covered that. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Maybe you did and I missed it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, how do the rankings of generals here correspond to the rankings of generals in the British or US Army? I see you have Lieutenant General, Colonel General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have the witness give the ascending order and then I could, if the Defence has no objection, attempt to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, would you please tell us in ascending order, going from the lowest to the highest, the General ranks, the ranks of General within the JNA and then the VRS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Army General, I do not think they had one of late.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the lowest rank of General within the JNA? That is called what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Major General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the next rank you would achieve as a General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lieutenant General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not here that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lieutenant General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the next rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, is there a higher rank than that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Army General, that is a four star General, but there was no Army General during the last 10 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Judge Vohrah, I can equate those if the Defence has no objection or we can call evidence on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: That is sufficient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry, that means you go Major General, Lieutenant General, Colonel General, do you, in ascending order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have that same anomaly, Judge Stephen, in that we go from a Major General to Lieutenant General, although in the officer ranks a Lieutenant is lower than a Major. At this time could both of those exhibits be returned to the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Should I explain perhaps the structure between Major and Lieutenant? I just heard the question. There are other ranks between Major and Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I know that but I believe Judge Vohrah's question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be an appropriate time to break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for lunch until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to resume?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Your Honour, prior to the break there was, perhaps, some uncertainty about two exhibits. I would like to have the witness shown both those exhibits and try to clarify that uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibits 169 and 170, please? (To the witness): Sir, if you would look first at Prosecution Exhibit 169, the chain of command of the Logistics system prior to 18th May? We have determined earlier that those individuals with double red Xs under their names are Serb officers from Serbia or Montenegro, and those individuals with a single red X under their names are Serb officers from Croatia or Slovenia. Looking at the officers on this chart that have no Xs under their names, how many of these officers are non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Among the non-Serb officers there are only two: myself, Colonel Selak, and Chief of the Technical Service Lieutenant Colonel Camic Mujo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could put this on the overhead perhaps it would assist the court. Sir, you have indicated that yourself, Colonel Selak, and Lieutenant Colonel Camic are non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to look at the remaining officers who have no X under their names: General Djukic, General Adzic and General Talic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These are Serb officers, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All three of these officers are from Bosnia-Herzegovina, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you would look at Prosecution Exhibit 170, if that could be put on the overhead? Again, if you would look only at the officers with no X or double X under their name, how many of those officers are non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am the only remaining one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then, sir, looking at the officers with no Xs under their name, that would be General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Djukic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Talic, Major Spiric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those officers are all Serb officers from Bosnia, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Those exhibits could be returned to the Registrar. Colonel Selak, I would like now to ask you some questions about combat units within your area. You have previously testified that the Banja Luka corps was located in your area of responsibility. Was that a JNA combat unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to 18th May 1992 what other JNA combat units were within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 5th Corps, the Rocket Brigade, the training centre for armoured and mechanized units. On Mount Kozara, north of Prijedor, there was a radar station. On that same Mount Kozara there was a relay centre of the Signals Regiment from Sarajevo, and the Logistics Base in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you also have an Air Force airfield in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Mahovljani airfield which was under the command of the Air Force of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Turning first to the Missile Brigade that you spoke of, to what command did this Missile Brigade belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Missile Brigade was under the direct command of the Commander of the 1st Military District in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then in 1992 when the Military Districts changed, to what command did that Rocket Brigade belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the command of the 2nd Military District, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was this Missile Brigade headquartered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Missile Brigade was headquartered at the Kozara barracks in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this an active duty or a reserve Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officers. It is an A unit, type A.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What do you mean by "type A unit"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Type A units were combat ready for use within 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Commander of this Brigade, if you know, was this an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And his ethnic group, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Novi Sad, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of missiles did this Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Russian type missiles, Lunar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are these missiles surface to air missiles or surface to surface missiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Surface to surface missiles.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The missiles for this site, where did the missiles themselves come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the former Soviet Union or Russia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So they would have come in through this Technical Administration branch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 was that Missile Brigade pulled out of the territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Missile Brigade had positions in the spring of 1992 in Banija near Glina and Petrinja. Later it returned to the region of Banja Luka. It had a battalion on Mount Vlasic towards Travnik, a battalion east of Banja Luka, 15 kilometres east, and a third in Banja Luka itself, I think.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 did that Missile Brigade leave your area or did it remain in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It remained within the region.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 did the Commander of that Brigade change or remain the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It remained the same.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May I ask a question, please, just regarding this? How long did that Brigade remain there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It remained for the duration of the war until I had left Banja Luka. It was still in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was the Commander of the Brigade the same person through that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the Commander of the Brigade left in the course of 1993. He went to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, you said that that Brigade remained in the area until you left Banja Luka. When was it that you left Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May 18th 1995.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have also mentioned a radar installation on Kozara Mountain; what command was that radar installation in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the Air Force and anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the Air Force in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Major General Ninkovic. I do not remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The radar installation itself, would this have been an active duty or a reserve unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exclusively active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: General Ninkovic, to your knowledge, was he an active duty officer or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Glamoc, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know who the Commander of the radar installation was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Concerning the signals radio station on Kozara Mountain, was that an active duty or a reserve unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty units.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What command were they in before 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the signals centre of the command of the 2nd Military District, Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Concerning the signals radio station, after 18th May 1992, did they remain in that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they remained.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The radar installation on Kozara Mountain, after 18th May, did it remain in that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Concerning the Air Force assets within your area of responsibility, you mentioned the airfield at Mahovljani. Where was Mahovljani in relation to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: North of Banja Luka, 20 kilometres on the road between Banja Luka and Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that airfield open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The airfield was officially opened in August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It was supplied with aircraft from where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the Soviet Union or Russia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of aircraft did they have at the airfield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know of the type, MIG 19, MIG 21, and I think there was one MIG 25. I have not seen it, I never saw it, but I heard of it. Whether it was permanently stationed at that airfield, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These MIG aircraft, were these fighter bomber aircraft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the fixed wing aircraft were any helicopters assigned to this airfield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The airfield itself and the assets at this airfield were JNA assets, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was the airfield supplied with munitions, bombs, the aeroplanes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Air Force independently contracted supplies, but I believe this was done through contracts between Yugoslavia and the Soviet Union, and the Air Force directly imported not just aircraft but other equipment for the Air Force from the Soviet Union.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This airfield at Mahovljani, where would the bombs for those aircraft have been brought in from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was another airfield there that was a JNA airfield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was a large airport in Bihac, one of the most modern ones, perhaps the third largest in Europe of its kind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992, did these Air Force assets remain at Mahovljani air Base?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, no, I mean 18th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These Air Force units that had been there, did the units also remain there after 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The airfield Base, Mahovljani, operated throughout the war and it is still operating. There were no planes flying, but the Base as a unit remained and they were on standby.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say that there were no planes flying. To your knowledge, did planes from this airfield take part in any attacks on non-Serb areas in Bosnia in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until the no-fly zone was established by the UN, planes did make regular combat flights towards Jajce, Travnik, Kotor Varos, Vitez in central Bosnia, and they acted in combat.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, how did you become aware of their combat activity in these areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Aeroplane bombs and other equipment withdrawn from Bihac was stored in the storage facility of Kremarica near Banja Luka and Kula near Mrkonjic Grad. The guards or the guards of the depots belonged to the Air Force. We gave them vehicles for the transport of bombs to the airfield.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992 did General Ninkovic remain in charge of the Air Force assets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about the units within the Banja Luka Corps itself. Before 18th May 1992, what active duty units belonged to the Banja Luka Corps or what was then known as the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty units or formation units, as we officially call them, were an Armoured Brigade; a Mechanized Brigade in Prijedor; a Mechanized Brigade in Derventa; the 16th Brigade in the Kozara barracks in Banja Luka; an Engineering Regiment in Banja Luka; a Mixed Artillery Regiment in Banja Luka; a mixed Armoured, Anti-armour Regiment in Banja Luka; a Signals Battalion in Banja Luka; a Military Police Battalion and the Logistics Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any type of anti-aircraft assets within the Banja Luka Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was an anti-aircraft battalion.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was armed -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I forgot to mention it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was armed with what type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had anti-aircraft guns and missiles arrow 2M or Strela 2M, of Soviet mix.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This mixed Artillery Regiment, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kozara barracks in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, the Commander of that Regiment, was that person active duty or reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (The answer was not audibly translated).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We did not get the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was certainly an active duty officer, a Lieutenant Colonel by rank.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was a Montenegrin but he was not a Bosnian, I am sure. He was not from Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This mixed Anti-armoured Artillery Regiment, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also at the Kozara barracks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, was the Commander of that Regiment an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was an active duty officer. I do not know who the Commander was because there were changes quite frequently. I do not know their names.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That was an active duty billet, an active duty slot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was an active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This Military Police Battalion, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Novi Logor barracks in Banja Luka near to the Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, the Commander of that unit, what was the person's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serb, a Major by rank. He came from Croatia. I do not know his surname.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This Anti-aircraft Battalion, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Battalion in the Kozara barracks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, the Commander of this Battalion, was this an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what was the ethnic group of this officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Serb, and he also came from Croatia. I do not know his name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The engineering regiment, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The units were located at the Kozara barracks and the engineering equipment of the regiment in the Trn settlement near Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Commander of this regiment, to your knowledge, was this an active duty or a reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, from Bijeljina in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, these units we have just spoken about, after 18th May 1992, did any of the Commanders of those units change?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not a single Commander was changed in that period.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you some questions about the brigades. You indicated that Banja Luka, Derventa and Prijedor had Mechanized Brigades. What types of weaponry would Mechanized Brigades have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mechanized Brigades had infantry, had infantry weapons, including machine guns, mortars, artillery up to 100 millimetres, cannons up to 100 millimetres and transport assets, that is, vehicles. That is why they are called "mechanized".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also indicated there was an Armoured Brigade in the 5th Corps. Where was that Armoured Brigade located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Armoured Brigade was in Kozara barracks in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know the numerical designation of that Armoured Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Each of these brigades, the Brigade in Banja Luka, all four of these Brigades, to your knowledge, were the commanders of each of these Brigades active duty officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all active duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the ethnic group of these Commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any of them Serbs from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that Celeketic of the 16th Brigade was from Serbia, and the Missile Brigade Commander, Colonel Obradov, was from Novi Sad. Colonel Arsic, Commander of the 343 Brigade in Prijedor, I am not sure about him, if he is from Serbia or Bosnia, but I still think he comes from Serbia because he spoke a dialect spoken in Serbia, but I am not positive about that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to these active duty units that you have mentioned, by the spring of 1992, would the Banja Luka Corps have had Territorial Defence Forces attached to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would it also have had the Light Brigades attached to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all reported to the Corps. It armed them, and they provided logistic support at the Rear Base in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, who was in control of military weaponry such as artillery, canons, tanks, rockets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards artillery, the Corps was in charge; for missiles, the Missiles Brigade supported directly to the command of the Military District in Sarajevo, and after 18th May to the main staff of the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was in control of military fixed wing aircraft and military helicopters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: General Ninkovic, the Commander of the Air Force, and his superior was General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was in control of military vehicles such as military trucks, armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Armoured vehicles or combat vehicles, Commander of units, the Corps Commander; motorized vehicles, unit Commanders of the lower rank from Company to Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, by the spring of 1992, had any such weaponry or vehicles been given to any Muslim groups by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, why should they?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 18th May, did the military remain in control of those weapons and equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When this alleged JNA withdrawal occurred, what was done with the JNA weapons, equipment and supplies in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The materiel that could not stay in the depots of the Base, because it was in the open, was transported to Serbia and Montenegro. The rest that could be stored under the roof protected remained in storage facilities of the Base or was given to the units.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So after 18th May 1992 the VRS took over control of these assets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When the JNA left Slovenia and Croatia, was it the JNA policy to leave its weapons, equipment and assets to the Croatians or the Slovenes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, the explicit order was that all assets had to be pulled out within the country, that was the official term, that is, to Bosnia, Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, are you aware of an instance in Croatia where a Commander left his weapons and equipment to the Croats when he and his troops withdrew from the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Varazdin, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he leave behind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is General Vasiljevic, yes. He left the complete Corps in Varazdin, which had tanks and artillery and all other materiel, so that men could leave Varazdin. So that the Corps was taken over by the Croatian army and the troops were set free; some came to Banja Luka, some continued to Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was any action taken against this Commander for what he did in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was brought to trial twice in Belgrade. He and Colonel Popov, Berislav Popov, his deputy, he spent in Banja Luka a short while and was then assigned to Belgrade and they were both convicted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the charges against them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: High treason, that he had surrendered war equipment, war assets to the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know what his term of imprisonment was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the Commander was sentenced to a term of 12 years of imprisonment. The Defence filed an appeal and there was a very hard debate about the trial in Yugoslavia. I believe the sentence was commuted to eight or nine years. I would not know the details.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, to your knowledge, was any one court martialled for leaving JNA assets in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the newly created VRS pay for any of the weapons, equipment or supplies left by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to talk you a bit about the Banja Luka Corps area of responsibility and chain of command.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, just one moment, Miss Hollis. If I may, I would like to ask the witness a couple of questions. I am not going to comment on that sound. (To the witness): Colonel Selak, from listening to your testimony, it appears that there were a number of brigades and units that were commanded by officers of the JNA, active officers, that is, officers who had active status as opposed to a reserve status, before May, 18th May 1992, and then after May 18th 1992 and after May 22nd 1992 they remained in those positions. Is that the gist of the testimony that you have given citing a number of instances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I asked you about one of them and I asked you if you knew how long that Commander remained in that position and you gave me an answer. I must admit, I do not remember; I think you said through the time that you were there, and that was 1995, December 1995 -- was it?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The witness would have to clarify that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In any case, you recall the question I asked you about whether you knew how long the Commander remained in that position? Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the Commander of the Armoured Brigade, Colonel Ratko Simic. He was the Brigade Commander from some time in 1989 until my departure from Banja Luka. He continued as a Commander of that Brigade. I had him in mind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: For the other Commanders whom you have mentioned, do you know how long they remained in that position other than the fact that they remained after May 22nd 1992?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to some of those we do have an exhibit that will respond to that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I was just trying to kind of wrap it up and understand the import of the testimony. Let me ask just one other question: If I understand your testimony this morning then, after the army became the army of the Republika Srspka -- and that would have been May 18th 1992 ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: -- then there was a change in their uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniform remained the same, but the insignia they had on their caps changed. There was a flag, blue/white/red and it first had "JNA" inscribed. After May 18th, this "JNA" letters were removed, and later on they wore on their left shoulder insignia in linen with "VRS" inscribed there, the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These Commanders, I gather, continued to be paid by the JNA; is that correct -- well, not actually the JNA but the official body that had paid the JNA before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty officers were throughout until my departure paid from Banja Luka, and the pensions to those who retired and lived in the Republika Srpska received their pensions from Belgrade, and even I received whatever is due me from Belgrade until December '95.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I have no additional questions. I am sorry to pre-empt your next exhibit, if that is what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Not at all, but I will move to that as an exhibit to help answer your question, your Honour. If I could have the document that shows the chain of command prior to 18th May? I would ask that this document be marked the next exhibit in line which, I believe, is Prosecution Exhibit 171 for identification. For the benefit of the Defence, this will be document 14 in the order of documents. (Exhibit 171 was handed to the witness) (To the witness): If I could ask you to look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes,.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Colonel Selak, does this document represent the chain of command of the Banja Luka Corps prior to 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender this as Prosecution Exhibit 171.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 171 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be put on the overhead, please? (To the witness): Sir, as we look at this depiction of the chain of command of the 5th Corps before 18th May 1992, we see then that General Talic is the Commander of the Corps, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you look at this chain of command chart that you have before you, how many officers shown on this chart are active duty officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are all active duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Looking at this chain of command, could you tell us how many of the officers shown on this chain of command are non-Serb officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Major Josip Loncar of anti-aircraft defence, and Chief for anti-nuclear, biological and chemical warfare, Lieutenant Colonel Muharem Puskar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I notice in the Corps combat units you have the Commander of the Derventa Brigade as an unknown person; does that mean you did not know his name, you do not remember his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, under -- of the Brigade in Derventa.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But it is correct that you do know he was a Serb officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We see for General Talic that his rank is marked as a general. In fact, is that a typographical error that we committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was my mistake. He is a Major General.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, once again looking at this exhibit, the double Xs once again mean that this is an officer from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The single X once again means this is a Serb officer from Croatia or Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: With the exception of Colonel Arsic, these remaining officers who are Serb officers that have no X under their name, these are Serb officers from Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is the Commander of the 16th Brigade was Colonel Celeketic, that is a missile unit but it is not part of the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Missile unit, is that the Missile Brigade you are talking about that you testified to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is the Missile Brigade which was not under the Corps command, but it was -- I included it in the flow chart not to forget it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is Colonel Obradov?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But the Commander of the 16th Mechanized Brigade was part of the 5th Corps, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was and still is a part of the 5th Corps. It is now the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So that if we are looking at this document again, with the exception of Major Loncar, Lieutenant Colonel Puskar, the individuals here who have no X under their names are Serb officers from Bosnia Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I had said with exception of Colonel Arsic, do you know where Colonel Arsic is from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Colonel Arsic, to my knowledge, and his manner of speech, I believe, comes from Serbia because he uses that dialect and the way of pronunciation. That is how we distinguish Serbians, Macedonians, Bosnians and others, but I cannot be positive about that. He is Serb and an active duty officer. I do believe he is from Serbia, but I say this with a reservation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would like to have this document marked as Prosecution Exhibit 172 for identification, please. This would be document 15 in the order of documents. (Exhibit 172 was handed to the witness) Colonel Selak, does this chart indicate the Banja Luka Corps chain of command after 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this again, the double red Xs are Serb officers from Serbia and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The single red Xs are Serb officers from Croatia or Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender this document as Prosecution Exhibit 172.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 172 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Sir, looking at this document at Prosecution Exhibit 172, how many officers on this document are active duty officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are all active duty officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Looking at this document, how many officers are non-Serb officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Chief of the Nuclear, Biological and Chemical Warfare -- I am sorry, but the microphone is switched off. We cannot hear the witness. Only Lieutenant Colonel Muharem Puskar, he was there until June 92 when he was replaced and went into retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You had mentioned on the earlier chart that Major Loncar was a non-Serb. In this chart who has replaced Major Loncar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The double Xs indicate that he is from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Sir, the dates under the names of officers on this chart, what do those dates signify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dates below indicate until when they held those posts. Colonel Stevilovic, Chief of Security in the Corps, was killed on the road between Celinic and Kotor Varos near Banja Luka after being ambushed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This happened in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know who ambushed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the road Banja Luka/Kotor Varos and on, in the direction of central Bosnia, there were no Muslim units. Colonel Stevilovic was an honest officer who fought against some irregularities in the Corps. There was a roadblock on the road and there were four officers in the car, or two officers and two persons from the security centre in Banja Luka. The official investigation and official press release is that they were Muslims, Muslim armed formations. However, I believe that he was killed by authorities because there had already been an attempt two months earlier on the Banja Luka/Jajce road at so-called Crna Rijeka, and I had drawn his attention that he had to take care of himself but, unfortunately, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There had been an earlier attempt against Colonel Stevilovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that earlier attempt two months before he was killed on the Banja Luka/Jajce road at the junction of roads of Mrkonjic. The place is called Crna Rijeka. There was this attempt to liquidate him, and when I heard about that I warned him to take care of himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This earlier attempt also occurred in an area controlled by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, controlled by the 5th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: These officers, other than Colonel Stevilovic, the dates under their names indicate the dates that they left their units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Looking at the Serb officers who had no dates under their names, what does that signify, the absence of dates under their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That during my active duty in Banja Luka in the Base they kept their posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I could provide another exhibit, please? This will be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 173 for identification, please? If that could be marked and provided to the witness? (Exhibit 173 was handed to the witness) For the Defence, this would be document 16 in the order of documents. Colonel Selak, does this document depict the chain of command from the 5th Corps upwards before 18th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is until May 18th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. Prior to May, to 18th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender that exhibit as Prosecution Exhibit 173.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 173 will be admitted.
